title.value: Send a daily Gmail summary to Slack

introduction.value: The poster uses a scheduled Codex automation to fetch unread Gmail messages and post a morning brief to Slack.

method.value: The poster set up a scheduled Codex automation as a morning brief that checks unread Gmail from a local-time window covering yesterday morning to now, then sends a Slack DM. The prompt tells the agent to paginate Gmail results, pull fields like sender, subject, snippet or body, recipients, thread ID, attachments and unsubscribe headers, classify each email into a fixed triage taxonomy, hide newsletters and sales, and stop after posting the brief until the user confirms any next step.

outcome.value: The result is a structured daily Slack summary of unread mail with counts by category and a tally of filtered newsletters and sales emails. The source does not report usage numbers or measured results, only the prompt and that the poster uses it for this non-coding task.

notes.value: One practical catch in the prompt is to omit Gmail maxResults because the poster says it caused intermittent 500 errors; paginate instead.

source_text.body:
Send a daily Gmail summary to Slack
The poster uses a scheduled Codex automation to fetch unread Gmail messages and post a morning brief to Slack.
Done with
CX
Codex
What they did
The poster set up a scheduled Codex automation as a morning brief that checks unread Gmail from a local-time window covering yesterday morning to now, then sends a Slack DM. The prompt tells the agent to paginate Gmail results, pull fields like sender, subject, snippet or body, recipients, thread ID, attachments and unsubscribe headers, classify each email into a fixed triage taxonomy, hide newsletters and sales, and stop after posting the brief until the user confirms any next step.
How it went
The result is a structured daily Slack summary of unread mail with counts by category and a tally of filtered newsletters and sales emails. The source does not report usage numbers or measured results, only the prompt and that the poster uses it for this non-coding task.
Worth knowing
One practical catch in the prompt is to omit Gmail maxResults because the poster says it caused intermittent 500 errors; paginate instead.
Try it yourself
with
Codex
Copy prompt
Every weekday at [time, timezone], fetch my unread Gmail from the last [24 hours] and write a brief of the important ones, grouped as needs reply, FYI and ignorable, with sender and one-line summaries. Post it to my Slack [channel or DM] and stop. Do not reply to, archive or delete any emails, and show me a sample brief before you turn on the schedule.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/PromptEngineering/comments/1tr11ui/i_found_a_prompt_that_makes_codex_better_at
